D2:177: Leiomyoma. A cell type benign neoplasm that is a benign tumor of smooth muscle cells. Synonyms: leiomyomatous neoplasm; leiomyomatous tumor.
D2:178: Silver-Russell Syndrome. A physical disorder that is characterized by severe intrauterine growth retardation, poor postnatal growth, craniofacial features such as a triangular shaped face and a broad forehead, body asymmetry, and a variety of minor malformations. Synonyms: Silver Russell Dwarfism.
D2:179: Aortic Valve Stenosis. An aortic valve disease that is characterized by narrowing of the heart's aortic valve opening. Synonyms: Aortic stenosis; Rheumatic aortic stenosis; rheumatic aortic valve stenosis.
D2:180: Vascular Diseases. A cardiovascular system disease that primarily affects the blood vessels which includes the arteries, veins and capillaries that carry blood to and from the heart. Synonyms: vascular tissue disease.
D2:181: Adenoma, Islet Cell. A pancreatic cystadenoma that is characterized by the overproduction of insulin. Synonyms: Insulin-Producing tumor of Islet cells; Islet cell adenoma.
D2:182: Rectal Neoplasms. A colorectal cancer that is located_in the rectum. Synonyms: cancer of rectum; carcinoma of rectum; carcinoma of the rectum; malignant neoplasm of rectum; malignant Rectal tumor.
D2:183: Choriocarcinoma. A placenta cancer that has_material_basis_in trophoblastic cells. Synonyms: Chorioepithelioma.
D2:184: Hepatitis B, Chronic. A viral hepatitis that results_in inflammation located_in liver, has_material_basis_in Hepatitis B virus (Orthohepadnavirus hominoidei), which is transmitted_by sexual contact, blood transfusions, or fomites like needles or syringes. The infection has_symptom fever, fatigue, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, clay-colored bowel movements, joint pain, and jaundice. Synonyms: chronic hepatitis B; hepatitis B infection; Serum hepatitis.
D2:186: Adenocarcinoma. A carcinoma that has_material_basis_in abnormally proliferating cells, derives_from epithelial cells, which originate in glandular tissue.
D2:187: Neoplasms, Germ Cell and Embryonal. A germ cell cancer that is derives_from a mixture of germs cells and embryonal cells. Synonyms: germ cell and embryonal neoplasm.
D2:188: Central Nervous System Diseases. A nervous system disease that affects either the spinal cord (myelopathy) or brain (encephalopathy) of the central nervous system.
D2:189: Meningioma. A central nervous system cancer that are manifested in the central nervous system and arise from the arachnoid cap cells of the arachnoid villi in the meninges. Synonyms: meningeal neoplasm; meningothelial cell tumor; neoplasm of the meninges; primary Meningeal tumor.
D2:191: Skin Diseases. An integumentary system disease that is located_in skin. Synonyms: Genodermatosis; skin and subcutaneous tissue disease.
D2:192: Trophoblastic Neoplasms. A germ cell and embryonal cancer that derives_from trophoblastic tissue. Synonyms: Trophoblastic tumor.
D2:194: Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome. A syndrome characterized by overgrowth (macrosomia), an increased risk of childhood cancer and congenital malformations.
D2:196: Hodgkin Disease. A lymphoma that is marked by the presence of a type of cell called the Reed-Sternberg cell. Synonyms: HL; Hodgkin lymphoma; Hodgkin's sarcoma; Hodgkins lymphoma; stage I Subdiaphragmatic Hodgkin Lymphoma.
D2:197: Polycythemia Vera. A myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by erythroid hyperplasia, myeloid leukocytosis, thrombocytosis, and splenomegaly. Synonyms: chronic erythremia; Osler-Vaquez syndrome; Polycythaemia rubra vera; Proliferative polycythaemia.
D2:198: Hyperhomocysteinemia. An amino acid metabolic disorder that involves an abnormally large level of homocysteine in the blood.
D2:200: Hydatidiform Mole. Synonyms: gestational trophoblastic neoplasia; molar pregnancy.
D2:203: Myocardial Ischemia. An artery disease that is characterized by plaque building up along the inner walls of the arteries of the heart resulting in a narrowing of the arteries and a reduced blood supply to the cardiac muscles. Synonyms: CHD; coronary arteriosclerosis; Coronary disease; coronary heart disease; Ischemic Heart Disease.
D2:207: Cardiomyopathies. A heart disease and a myopathy that is characterized by deterioration of the function of the heart muscle.
D2:208: Diffuse Intrinsic Pontine Glioma. A histone mutated tumor that is characterized by loss of histone H3 p.K28me3 (K27me3) methylation and located throughout the midline structures of the central nervous system. Methylation loss may be due to p.K28M (K27M) mutation in one of the histone H3 isoforms (H3.1, H3.2, or H3.3), overexpression of EZHIP, or mutation of the EGFR gene. Synonyms: diffuse midline glioma, EGFR-mutant; diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27M-mutant; diffuse midline glioma, H3-wildtype with EZHIP overexpression.
D2:209: Celiac Disease. An autoimmune disease of gastrointestinal tract that is caused by a reaction located_in small intestine to gliadin, a prolamin (gluten protein) found in wheat, and similar proteins found in the crops of the tribe Triticeae. The disease is associated with HLA-DQ gene. It has_symptom abdominal pain, has_symptom constipation, has_symptom diarrhea, has_symptom nausea and vomiting, and has_symptom loss of appetite. Synonyms: celiac sprue; coeliac disease; idiopathic steatorrhea.
D2:210: Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome. A Human immunodeficiency virus infectious disease that results_in reduction in the numbers of CD4-bearing helper T cells below 200 per microliter of blood or 14% of all lymphocytes thereby rendering the subject highly vulnerable to life-threatening infections and cancers, has_material_basis_in Human immunodeficiency virus 1 (Lentivirus humimdef1) or Human immunodeficiency virus 2 (Lentivirus humimdef2), which are transmitted_by sexual contact, transmitted_by transfer of blood, semen, vaginal fluid, pre-ejaculate, or breast milk, transmitted_by congenital method, and transmitted_by contaminated needles. Opportunistic infections are common in people with AIDS. Synonyms: acquired Immune deficiency; acquired immune deficiency syndrome; AIDS.
D2:211: Spondylitis, Ankylosing. An arthritis that results_in inflammation in the joints of the spine and pelvis. The disease has_symptom pain, has_symptom stiffness in the spine, has_symptom stiffness in the neck, has_symptom stiffness in the hips, has_symptom stiffness in the jaw and has_symptom stiffness in the rib cage. Synonyms: Bekhterev syndrome; Bekhterev's disease; Marie-Strumpell disease.
D2:212: HELLP Syndrome. A severe pre-eclampsia characterized by hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme and low platelet count.
D2:213: Aortic Aneurysm, Thoracic. An aortic aneurysm that is located_in the thoracic aorta.
D2:215: Osteonecrosis. An ischemic bone disease that results_in necrosis located_in bone. Synonyms: aseptic necrosis; Avascular necrosis of bone; bone necrosis.
D2:216: Silicosis. A pneumoconiosis that is an inflammation and scarring of the upper lobes of the lungs causing nodular lesions resulting from inhalation of silica, quartz or slate particles. Synonyms: Pneumoconiosis due to silicates; Silica pneumoconiosis; Silicotic fibrosis of lung; silicotuberculosis.
D2:217: Lemierre Syndrome. A commensal bacterial infectious disease that is characterized by systemic sepsis, ulcerative or necrotic lesions and multisystem abscesses caused by Fusobacterium necrophorum. The disease often first presents as a severe tonsillitis or pharyngitis with high-grade fever and chills together with leukocytosis, cervical pain and neck swelling. Synonyms: acute sore throat; human necrobacillosis; postanginal sepsis.
D2:218: Hepatitis C. A viral hepatitis that results_in inflammation located_in liver, has_material_basis_in hepatitis C virus (Hepacivirus hominis), which is transmitted_by blood from an infected person enters the body of an uninfected person. The infection has_symptom fever, has_symptom fatigue, has_symptom loss of appetite, has_symptom nausea, has_symptom vomiting, has_symptom abdominal pain, has_symptom clay-colored bowel movements, has_symptom joint pain, and has_symptom jaundice. Synonyms: chronic hepatitis C; hepatitis C infection; hepatitis nonA nonB; NANBH; Viral hepatitis C.
D2:223: Adenocarcinoma, Mucinous. An adenocarcinoma that derives_from epithelial cells originating in glandular tissue, which produce mucin. Synonyms: mucin-producing adenocarcinoma; Mucin-Secreting adenocarcinoma; Mucin-Secreting carcinoma; Mucous carcinoma; Pseudomyxoma peritonei with unknown primary site.
D2:224: Bone Neoplasms. A connective tissue cancer that is located_in bone and is characterized by uncontrolled cellular proliferation that destroys normal bone tissue. Synonyms: bone neoplasm; bone tumour; CA - bone cancer; malignant bone neoplasm; malignant bone tumour.
D2:225: Myasthenia Gravis. An autoimmune disease of the nervous system that has_material_basis_in antibodies to acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, has_symptom ptosis, has_symptom diplopia, has_symptom dysphagia, has_symptom dysarthria, has_symptom muscle weakness and has_symptom shortness of breath.
D2:226: Thyroiditis, Autoimmune. An autoimmune disease of endocrine system that involves inflammation located_in thyroid gland caused by the immune system reacting against its own tissues. Synonyms: Chronic Lymphocytic Thyroiditis; Hashimoto thyroiditis; Hashimoto's Disease; Hashimoto's syndrome; Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
D2:227: Diabetes Mellitus, Type 1. A diabetes mellitus that is characterized by destruction of pancreatic beta cells resulting in absent or extremely low insulin production. Synonyms: IDDM; insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus; type I diabetes mellitus.
D2:229: Cataract. A lens disease characterized by clouding of the lens inside the eye which leads to a decrease in vision.
D2:232: Rhinitis, Allergic. A rhinitis that is an allergic inflammation and irritation of the nasal airways involving sneezing, runny nose, nasal congestion, itching and tearing of the eyes caused by exposure to an allergen such as pollen, dust, mold, animal dander and droppings of cockroaches or house dust mites. Synonyms: atopic rhinitis; hay fever; Non-seasonal allergic rhinitis; Perenial allergic rhinitis; pollenosis.
D2:233: Chordoma. A notochordal cancer that derives_from cellular remnants of the notochord. Synonyms: notochordoma.
D2:235: Pemphigus. An autoimmune disease of skin and connective tissue that is characterized by blistering of the outer layer of the skin and mucous membranes (mouth, nose, throat, eyes, and genitals), causing lesions and blisters that are easily ruptured.
D2:237: Kidney Diseases. A urinary system disease that is located_in the kidney. Synonyms: impaired renal function disease; nephropathy.
D2:238: Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease. A steatotic liver disease characterized by at least one of five specified cardiometabolic risk factors and no other discernible cause with normal to no alcohol use. The five cardiometabolic risk factors are: (1) higher than normal body mass index or waist circumference; (2) higher than normal serum glucose or glycated hemoglobin level, or type 2 diabetes; (3) higher than normal blood pressure or hypertensive treatment; (4) higher than normal plasma triglycerides or lipid lowering treatment; and (5) lower than normal plasma high-density lipoprotein cholesterol. Synonyms: MAFLD; MASLD; metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease; metabolic dysfunction-related steatotic liver disease; metabolic-associated fatty liver disease.
D2:239: Exfoliation Syndrome. A phacogenic glaucoma that is characterized by open-angle glaucoma related to deposition of extracellular fibrillar material in anterior segment structures, which blocks aqueous fluid outflow, raises intraocular pressure, and leads to eventual optic nerve atrophy and visual field loss. Exfoliation syndrome has_symptom progressive decreased vision, especially peripheral vision. Exfoliation syndrome is caused by age-related deposition of fibrillar material in anterior segment structures. Synonyms: Pseudoexfoliation glaucoma; Pseudoexfoliation syndrome.
D2:241: Fibroma. A connective tissue benign neoplasm composed of fibrous or connective tissues that derives_from mesenchymal tissue.
D2:242: Diabetes, Gestational. A diabetes mellitus that manifests during pregnancy. Synonyms: GDM; Gestational diabetes mellitus; Maternal gestational diabetes mellitus.
D2:244: Hepatitis. A liver disease that is characterized as an inflammation of the liver. Synonyms: acute and subacute liver necrosis; acute hepatitis; acute/subac. necrosis of liver; animal hepatitis; chronic hepatitis.
D2:245: Hemangioma, Capillary. A hemangioma that is characterized by the presence of capillary-sized vascular channels without prominent epithelioid endothelial cells. Synonyms: Capillary haemangioma; cellular hemangioma of Infancy; Congenital vascular hamartoma; Congenital vascular naevus; Infantile hemangioma.
D2:246: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis. A frontotemporal dementia and/or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis that has_material_basis_in heterozygous mutation in CHMP2B on 3p11.2. Synonyms: ALS17; AMYOTROPHIC LATERAL SCLEROSIS 17 (FORMERLY); amyotrophic lateral sclerosis type 17; CHMP2B-RELATED; CHMP2B-related frontotemporal dementia.
D2:247: Fibrosarcoma. A connective tissue cancer that has_material_basis_in fibrous connective tissue and characterized by the presence of immature proliferating fibroblasts or undifferentiated anaplastic spindle cells in a storiform pattern. Synonyms: Fibrocytic tumor; fibrosarcoma of soft tissue; fibrous tissue neoplasm.
D2:248: Uterine Neoplasms. A female reproductive organ cancer that is located_in the uterus. Synonyms: CA - cancer of uterus; malignant neoplasm of uterus; malignant uterine tumor; neoplasm of uterus; Tumour of uterus.
D2:249: Pulmonary Fibrosis. An interstitial lung disease that is characterized by destruction, scarring, and thickening of the interstitial lung tissues and progressive pulmonary function loss in a restrictive pattern, has_symptom progressive shortness of breath, fatigue, and chronic cough, possibly has_material_basis_in exposure to certain chemicals, autoimmune conditions, and radiation. It can be caused by inhaling hazardous chemicals, certain diseases, medication and genetics or unknown causes. Synonyms: Fibrosis of lung.
D2:251: Sarcoma, Endometrial Stromal. An endometrial stromal tumor that has_material_basis_in connective tissue. Synonyms: endometrial stromal sarcoma, high grade; ESS; Undifferentiated endometrial sarcoma.
D2:252: Osteolysis, Essential. A syndrome that is characterized by bone loss (osteolysis) which is often associated with swelling or abnormal blood vessel growth (angiomatous proliferation). Bone loss can occur in just one bone or spread to soft tissue and adjacent bones. Synonyms: Disappearing bone disease; essential osteolysis; Gorham disease; Gorham-Stout Syndrome; massive osteolysis.
D2:253: Retinal Degeneration. A retinal disease that is characterized by deterioration of the retina caused by the progressive and eventual death of the cells of the retina. Synonyms: degeneration of retina.
D2:255: Diabetic Retinopathy. Synonyms: Retinal abnormality - diabetes-related.
D2:256: Vitreoretinopathy, Proliferative. A retinal and vitreous disease characterized by ocular inflammation, vascular dropout, large spots of hyperpigmentation, neovascularization of the peripheral and posterior retina, vitreous hemorrhage, and retinal detachment that has_material_basis_in heterozygous mutation in the CAPN5 gene on chromosome 11q13.5. Synonyms: ADNIV; autosomal dominant neovascular inflammatory vitreoretinopathy; proliferative vitreoretinopathy; Retinitis proliferans.
D2:257: Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia. A lung disease that is characterized by underdeveloped lungs in newborns that can be easily irritated or inflamed after birth resulting in damage to the alveoli of the lungs and bronchi. Most newborns who develop BPD are born more than 10 weeks before their due dates, weigh less than 2 pounds at birth, and have breathing problems. Synonyms: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia of newborn; Chronic lung disease of prematurity; Neonatal chronic lung disease; neonatal chronic respiratory disease; Perinatal bronchopulmonary dysplasia.
D2:265: Myelodysplastic Syndromes. A bone marrow cancer that is characterized by under production of white blood cells, red blood cells and platelets.
D2:267: Carcinoma, Islet Cell. An islet cell tumor that has_material_basis_in epithelial cells. Synonyms: carcinoma of endocrine pancreas; Islet cell carcinoma; malignant neoplasm of islets of Langerhans; pancreatic neuroendocrine carcinoma.
D2:268: Rhabdomyosarcoma, Embryonal. A rhabdomyosarcoma wherein the mesenchymally-derived malignant cells resemble the primitive developing skeletal muscle of the embryo; it occurs most often in the head and neck area or in the genital or urinary organs.
D2:269: Heart Valve Diseases. A heart disease involving one or more of the four valves of the heart (the aortic and mitral valves on the left and the pulmonary and tricuspid valves on the right). Synonyms: Valvular heart disease.
D2:270: Liver Diseases. Synonyms: disorder of liver; hepatic disorder.
D2:272: Hypertension, Pulmonary. A hypertension characterized by an increase of blood pressure in the pulmonary artery, pulmonary vein or pulmonary capillaries.
D2:274: Heroin Dependence. An opiate dependence that involves the continued use of heroin despite problems related to use of the substance.
D2:276: Syndrome. A disease characterized by a group of signs and symptoms that occur together and characterize a particular abnormality.
D2:278: Cardiomyopathy, Dilated. An intrinsic cardiomyopathy that is characterized by an an enlarged heart and damage to the myocardium causing the heart to pump blood inefficiently. Synonyms: Congestive cardiomyopathy; Familial dilated cardiomyopathy; Idiopathic dilation cardiomyopathy; primary dilated cardiomyopathy.
D2:279: Substance-Related Disorders. A disease of mental health involving the abuse or dependence on a substance that is ingested in order to produce a high, alter one's senses, or otherwise affect functioning.
D2:281: Nephrolithiasis. A kidney disease characterized by the formation of stoney concentrations in the kidneys. Synonyms: kidney stones; Stone - kidney/ureter.
D2:282: Burkitt Lymphoma. A mature B-cell neoplasm of B-cells found in the germinal center. Synonyms: Burkitt lymphoma/leukaemia; Burkitt's Lymphoma; Burkitt's tumor; Burkitt's tumor or lymphoma; malignant lymphoma, Burkitt's type.
D2:283: Myopia. A refractive error characterized by the inability to see farther objects clearly. Synonyms: near vision; near-sightedness; short-sightedness.
D2:288: Multiple Sclerosis, Relapsing-Remitting. A multiple sclerosis that is characterized by relapse (attacks of symptom flare-ups) followed by remission (periods of recovery). Symptoms may vary from mild to severe, and relapses and remissions may last for days or months. More than 80 percent of people who have MS begin with relapsing-remitting cycles. Synonyms: Relapsing-remitting MS; RRMS.
D2:289: Frontotemporal Dementia. A frontotemporal dementia and/or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis that has_material_basis_in heterozygous mutation in CHMP2B on 3p11.2. Synonyms: ALS17; AMYOTROPHIC LATERAL SCLEROSIS; AMYOTROPHIC LATERAL SCLEROSIS 17 (FORMERLY); amyotrophic lateral sclerosis type 17; CHMP2B-RELATED.
D2:292: Scleroderma, Systemic. A scleroderma that is characterized by fibrosis (or hardening) of the skin and major organs, as well as vascular alterations, and autoantibodies. Synonyms: progressive systemic sclerosis; Scleroderma; Scleroderma syndrome; systemic sclerosis.
D2:293: Narcolepsy. A sleep disorder that involves an excessive urge to sleep at inappropriate times, such as while at work. Synonyms: Narcolepsy, without cataplexy; paroxysmal sleep.
D2:295: Psoriasis. A skin disease that is characterized by patches of thick red skin and silvery scales.
D2:296: Asthma. A bronchial disease that is characterized by chronic inflammation and narrowing of the airways, which is caused by a combination of environmental and genetic factors. The disease has_symptom recurring periods of wheezing (a whistling sound while breathing), has_symptom chest tightness, has_symptom shortness of breath, has_symptom mucus production and has_symptom coughing. Synonyms: bronchial hyperreactivity; chronic obstructive asthma; chronic obstructive asthma with acute exacerbation; chronic obstructive asthma with status asthmaticus.
D2:297: Plasmacytoma. Synonyms: Myeloma - solitary; Myeloma, solitary; Solitary myeloma; Solitary plasmacytoma.
D2:298: Cleft Lip. An orofacial cleft that is characterized by a congenital defect in the upper lip where the maxillary prominence fails to merge with the merged medial nasal prominences. Synonyms: cheiloschisis; cleft lip, unilateral, complete; complete unilateral cleft lip; hare lip; Labium leporinum.
D2:299: Neurodegenerative Diseases. A central nervous system disease that results in the progressive deterioration of function or structure of neurons. Synonyms: degenerative disease.
D2:300: Angelman Syndrome. A syndrome that is characterized by delayed development, intellectual disability, severe speech impairment, and problems with movement and balance. Synonyms: happy puppet syndrome; puppetlike syndrome.
D2:301: Teratocarcinoma. A mixed germ cell tumor that is a mixture of teratoma with embryonal carcinoma, or with choriocarcinoma, or with both. Synonyms: mixed Embryonal carcinoma and teratoma.
D2:302: Anemia, Aplastic. A normocytic anemia that is characterized by a deficiency of red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets produced by bone marrow.
D2:303: Dyskeratosis Congenita. A skin disease characterized by cutaneous pigmentation, premature graying, dystrophy of the nails, leukoplakia of the oral mucosa, continuous lacrimation due to atresia of the lacrimal ducts, often thrombocytopenia, anemia, testicular atrophy in the male carriers and predisposition to cancer. Synonyms: DKCD.
D2:304: Mucocutaneous Lymph Node Syndrome. A lymphadenitis characterized by swelling of cervical lymph nodes in infants and young children and inflammation of medium-sized blood vessels and that symptoms of fever, congestion of ocular conjunctivae, reddening of lips, reddening of oral cavity, protuberance of tongue papillae and edema of extremities. Synonyms: acute febrile MCLS; acute febrile mucocutaneous lymph node syndrome; Kawasaki's disease; MLNS.
D2:305: Adrenal Gland Neoplasms. An endocrine gland cancer located_in the adrenal glands which are located above the kidneys. Synonyms: adrenal cancer; adrenal neoplasm; malignant Adrenal tumor; malignant neoplasm of adrenal gland; neoplasm of adrenal gland.
D2:306: Hypopharyngeal Neoplasms. A pharynx cancer that is located_in the hypopharynx. Synonyms: Hypopharyngeal cancer; malignant Hypopharyngeal tumor; malignant neoplasm of hypopharynx; malignant tumor of hypopharynx; malignant tumour of hypopharynx.
D2:308: Klinefelter Syndrome. A chromosomal duplication syndrome that is characterized by infertility and that has_material_basis_in an extra X chromosome in cells in men. Synonyms: 47, XXY; Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism; Klinefelter's syndrome; XXY syndrome; XXY trisomy.
